(a) In General.—Clause (iv) of section 170(e)(3)(C) is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to contributions made after December 31, 2011.

fable.w: This section only extends a date in a tax code provision and sets an effective date for contributions. The word "contributions" could be mistaken for outside-party involvement, but it refers to charitable contributions for tax deduction purposes, not to any consultation, comment, hearing, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: Clause (iv) of section 170(e)(3)(C) is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.

qwen_block.w: This section merely amends a date in the Internal Revenue Code regarding tax deductions for contributions. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or required interactions with states, tribes, or the public mentioned.
qwen_block.s:
(a) In General.—Clause (iv) of section 170(e)(3)(C) is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to contributions made after December 31, 2011.

opus.w: This section only moves a tax provision's expiration date from December 31, 2011 to December 31, 2013 and says which contributions the change applies to. Here "contributions" means charitable donations, not outside parties giving input on a federal decision. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends a statutory deadline for charitable contributions and specifies the effective date of that amendment. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with or participate in a federal decision. The only actors involved are Congress (making the law) and the entities governed by the Internal Revenue Code, but no participatory process is described.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the date for charitable contributions involves public participation because it affects the general public's tax behavior. However, the text itself only describes a legislative amendment to a deadline and its effective date. It does not establish any process for the public to consult with, comment on, or participate in the decision-making process regarding this change. The actors involved are Congress (amending the law) and the IRS (implicitly, via the code section), which are inside the federal government. There is no mention of hearings, comment periods, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states or tribes.
